boards.title: Your First Weekend at Saint Joseph's University - Philadelphia, Shared as Cards
boards.description: A grounded first-weekend sequence that starts on Hawk Hill, makes room for recreation and reflection, then heads into Philadelphia for a daytime market visit.

cards.title: Start by getting your bearings
cards.subtitle: A self-guided walk across Hawk Hill
cards.notes: Open the current Hawk Hill map and walk between the labeled academic, student-life, recreation and green-space landmarks before making off-campus plans.
cards.short_summary: A practical first pass through the campus you will use every day.
cards.evidence_claim: Saint Joseph's current Hawk Hill campus map identifies campus destinations, paths, parking and the nearby SEPTA Overbrook Station.
cards.access_notes: Use the current map for wayfinding; individual building access can vary.

cards.title: Find the student-life hub
cards.subtitle: Hawk Hill Campus • map location E2
cards.notes: Stop at Campion to locate Student Life, Inclusion and Diversity, The Pod and its other listed services, then save the building as a meet-up point.
cards.short_summary: A central named building for locating student-facing services.
cards.evidence_claim: The Hawk Hill campus map lists Campion Student Center and identifies Student Life, Inclusion and Diversity, The Pod, Saxbys and Doyle Banquet Hall there.
cards.access_notes: Check building access and service availability with Saint Joseph's University.

cards.title: Make a library support plan
cards.subtitle: Hawk Hill Campus • library and learning commons
cards.notes: Walk through Drexel Library and identify a service desk; bookmark the library page so you can return for research help, workshops and campus resources.
cards.short_summary: A first-weekend setup stop for academic support and future research.
cards.evidence_claim: Saint Joseph's describes Francis A. Drexel Library as a center for research, collaboration and scholarship, with research, tutoring and writing support.
cards.access_notes: Library services and building hours may change; consult the library before visiting.

cards.title: Scope out a future group-work spot
cards.subtitle: Hawk Hill Campus • connected to Drexel Library
cards.notes: Find the Post Learning Commons and note its atrium, lounges and terrace; use the reservation process later when your group needs a project space.
cards.short_summary: A named campus setting for collaboration after the first weekend.
cards.evidence_claim: Saint Joseph's says the Post Learning Commons and Drexel Library provide meeting and event spaces, and that study rooms are available for groups of two or more.
cards.access_notes: Student reservations are required for some spaces; check the library's room-reservation guidance.

cards.title: Try a daytime recreation option
cards.subtitle: Maguire Campus • fitness and recreation facility
cards.notes: Visit O'Pake during its posted operating hours to see the pool, courts and fitness areas, then check Campus Recreation for an activity that fits your schedule.
cards.short_summary: A campus recreation stop with several ways to get active.
cards.evidence_claim: Saint Joseph's states that the renovated O'Pake Fitness & Recreation Center has a pool, basketball courts, fitness center and Campus Recreation programs.
cards.access_notes: The facility is presented for SJU students; confirm current operating hours and program eligibility before going.

cards.title: Take a quiet museum pause
cards.subtitle: Barnes Arboretum area • Saint Joseph's University
cards.notes: Choose a gallery visit or a listed museum program, and leave time to look closely at a few works rather than trying to see everything at once.
cards.short_summary: A campus art stop that can anchor a slower afternoon.
cards.evidence_claim: Saint Joseph's lists the Frances M. Maguire Art Museum's exhibitions and recurring offerings including family programs, fiber-art days, yoga and music events.
cards.source_title: Frances M. Maguire Art Museum Events
cards.access_notes: The museum lists public hours; review its events page for current hours and program details.

cards.entity_name: Barnes Arboretum at Saint Joseph's University
cards.title: Walk the arboretum grounds
cards.subtitle: 50 Lapsley Lane, Merion • Saint Joseph's University
cards.notes: Pick up a map-guide at the Welcome Center and take a quiet walk on the grounds; stay on paths, leave plant material in place and take personal photos respectfully.
cards.short_summary: A free, map-guided outdoor reset beside campus.
cards.evidence_claim: Saint Joseph's states that entry to the Barnes Arboretum is free, requires no reservations or tickets, and offers map-guides at the Welcome Center.
cards.source_title: The Barnes Arboretum at Saint Joseph's University
cards.access_notes: Normally open daily except when the University is closed; confirm current hours before visiting.

cards.title: Locate a reflection space
cards.subtitle: Hawk Hill Campus • map location E2
cards.notes: Find the Chapel of St. Joseph during your campus walk so you know where it is for services, reflection or a calm pause when programming is available.
cards.short_summary: A named campus chapel to orient yourself to early in the term.
cards.evidence_claim: The Hawk Hill campus map identifies the Chapel of St. Joseph at map location E2.
cards.access_notes: Access and service schedules vary; consult Campus Ministry or the University calendar.

cards.title: Find the athletics landmark
cards.subtitle: Athletic Center • Hawk Hill Campus
cards.notes: Walk past Hagan Arena and the Athletic Center to place a major campus landmark on your mental map; check the official athletics calendar for public events.
cards.short_summary: A clearly marked campus venue to recognize before an event day.
cards.evidence_claim: The current Hawk Hill campus map lists Hagan Arena within the Athletic Center.
cards.access_notes: Event entry, ticketing and access depend on the specific event.

cards.title: Finish with a daytime Philadelphia market visit
cards.subtitle: Center City Philadelphia • public market
cards.notes: Head in during the Market's posted daytime hours, walk a full lap before choosing a merchant, and check individual vendor hours if you plan to eat there.
cards.short_summary: A central-city food-and-shopping stop supported by official visitor guidance.
cards.evidence_claim: Reading Terminal Market says it is open daily 8 a.m.–6 p.m., with individual merchant hours varying, and is reachable by train, bus, subway, bike, car, rideshare or on foot.
cards.access_notes: Market hours are 8 a.m.–6 p.m. daily except listed holidays; individual merchant hours vary.
